# ECDEV registry/domain qualification analysis

Read-only at central main `69b0b9868fecce5c9b8ff2360c6d7db4300fb60c`. No repository edits or Cargo/source execution. Exact supporting blobs/raw hashes and source artifact provenance are in `evidence.json`.

## Concrete invariants and coupling

`core/semantic/src/schema.rs:642–647` defines SHARDS as physical sources of Chronica, not independent sovereign domains. Its domain is a semantic prefix for legacy importer proposals, never a repository-name prefix. Current rows at 653–689 are empty for Ynventa/Chronica, compiler for Atlas, connector for UC, commerce for Esellios, finance for Fi-game, machine for Mechatron. `shard(id)` is an exact ID lookup; `shard_of_origin` at 696–700 compares the complete owner/repository string with ASCII case-insensitivity. It does not normalize arbitrary URLs, trim whitespace or verify forge ownership. Atlas `git_origin` at 77–98 separately extracts owner/repository through `oss_key`; do not conflate remote parsing with registry origin comparison. Preserve original origin bytes and bind normalized comparison separately. Blank/foreign or ID/origin mismatches must be refused by the new qualifier, not assigned a fallback identity.

All direct Shard.domain value uses found in core/apps/substrate reduce to Atlas importer lookup at `apps/cli/src/migration/atlas/mod.rs:242` and schema serialization at `apps/cli/src/protocol.rs:286–290`. Importer `qualify` at 197–201 concatenates domain.local. `node_for` at 148–177 handles ambiguous local proposals via path-derived fallback and a per-import `taken` set; it does not compare other source graphs. Ynventa projection keys instead become ynventa.<shard>. Existing declarations are not globally rewritten when the registry domain changes. Scaffold at 33–37 and importer at 216–220 explicitly refuse ECDEV before inference/write, including forced registration; adding a row cannot authorize this lossy path.

No executable uniqueness requirement for domain strings was found. Two existing empty domains already refute universal domain uniqueness. Sharing commerce is structurally representable and consistent with semantics; it is not proof that all resulting keys/owners are collision-free. A new automatic uniqueness restriction would be new policy rather than reuse of an existing invariant. Conversely, choosing a novel repository-name prefix solely to avoid collisions violates the semantic intent and can rekey source meanings.

A registry row changes rendered protocol schema text, therefore schema digest and exact engine binding/locks/snapshots and coordinated consumer interpretation. Capsule carries shard/origin and schema/engine binding (`substrate/linker/src/capsule.rs:52–58,150–151`), not a separately enforced domain ownership partition. Workspace at `apps/cli/src/cli/mod.rs:2041+` and scheduling at `apps/cli/src/schedule/mod.rs:77` enumerate registered shards; linker missing-source denominator at `substrate/linker/src/linker.rs:333` likewise changes. Seven-source assertions such as `apps/cli/tests/organism.rs:1167+` and protocol schema count assertions require deliberate updates and actual checks. These are already authorized engineering tasks, not reasons to seek a new architecture decision.

Canonical identity is H(namespace, semantic_key), with namespaces chronica/oss/external, never repository (`apps/cli/src/conformance/mod.rs:229–235`). Linker refuses unknown shards, schema mismatch and duplicate shards; same-schema engine skew is currently a SUBSYSTEM_SKEW warning (line 326), not a universal hard refusal. It also detects two physical/technology owners of the same Chronica identity (`substrate/linker/src/linker.rs:295–360`). Shared domains neither create a second identity namespace nor permit two physical owners. Existing absorption domain routing is its own rule set (`substrate/extinction/src/absorption.rs:145–210`); it does not derive permission from SHARDS.domain.
